A waifu is more of a sacred concept, much like how you may have a 'baby' of a car. You may like other cars, but no car will ever compare to "Your Baby". You will do anything possible to get "Your Baby" up and running again.

In the same vein, a 'waifu' is an idealized version of a mate, usually a character from an anime or manga series. It can be summed up in the phrase "Do it for her." A NEET might not self-improve, simply for their own sake, but they will self-improve for the sake of the supposed happiness of their 'waifu'. He is doing better for himself, so she is happy for him. Also importantly, it's generally frowned upon, much like polygamy, to take more than one 'waifu', because that implies that your affections are split multiple ways.

If you're familiar with the type of talk that goes on on the /x/ boards, it's kind of like a more platonic version of a tulpa. Some anons fap to their waifu, some anons see it as 'soiling' the idea of her to use as fap fuel, but the central concept is based around the concept of an idea to love and hold sacred as someone to look up to, and improve yourself, because it would make them happy to see you improving. Many anons will even have a picture (usually a wall-scroll or similar other merchandise) or a figurine of their waifu for a physical presence in their lives, and as a reminder that "She's always watching" as a way to ping their conscience whenever they're tempted to do something they know is wrong, and would draw the disapproval of their waifu. It's a concept that tends to be focused primarily on single, forever-alone Anons, but is not exempt to them, as some Anons that have significant others may also have a waifu. So they form a mental/emotional companion, moral compass guidepost, and inspiration for self-improvement, all in one concept, as a mental construct.

So, in essence, asking "What is your favorite waifu," is a bit like asking you who your favorite wife is. It's a question that presupposes having more than one. "Who is your waifu," would be a much more accurate question, and the answer would differ, depending on the tastes and needs of the anon in question. Those that need more spurring-to-action might have a more tsundere-type like Rin Tohsaka (Fate Stay/Night), whilst those with a more nurturing and protective emotional need might have, say Nodoka Miyazaki (Negima?!).
